headline: Philadelphia Indigenous Group Restores Native Crops on City Lots
meta_description: An Indigenous group in Philadelphia has transformed vacant lots into native gardens, reviving endangered Lenape corn and Nanticoke squash.
summary_short: An Indigenous group in Philadelphia has transformed three vacant lots into native gardens, bringing back endangered Lenape corn and Nanticoke squash to the city.
body:
An Indigenous group in Philadelphia has transformed three vacant lots into native gardens, reviving endangered Lenape corn and Nanticoke squash while creating food and shelter for local wildlife.

The project reclaims space in the city to grow crops historically cultivated by the region's first peoples. By restoring these traditional varieties, the group is both preserving Indigenous agricultural knowledge and addressing food access in their community.

The gardens serve a dual purpose: they provide nourishment for humans and create habitat for local birds and pollinators. What began as reclaiming abandoned urban land has become a living bridge to the past—one planted lot at a time.
quick_facts: Three vacant lots in Philadelphia transformed into native gardens
Endangered Lenape corn and Nanticoke squash now growing in the city
Gardens create food and shelter for local wildlife
